notes: The chronogram is śiśu-svāda-sindhu. Taking śiśu as an error for śaśi (=1), svāda=rasa (=6) and sindhu (=7), and reading right to left, the year is NS 761. With the sun in Makara this is about January 1641 CE. This conflicts with the stated reign of Jagatprakāśamalla of Bhaktapur, who acceded c. NS 764 / 1644 CE. Either śiśu stands for a different number, the year is misread, or the king is named anachronistically. The weekday was not checked. The locatives dīnādhināthe kamanīyavarṇe deśapradhāne sukṛtaikarāśau grammatically continue the king's epithets. Still, 'deśapradhāna' might be meant for Dhanasiṃha, who could be a pradhāna (minister); if so, his role may be 'minister' as well. The scribe's name is marked (!) by the cataloguer: 'Kutu' is doubtful, possibly Kuṭu or Khuṭu. The text copied is the Kāśīkhaṇḍa of the Skandapurāṇa.
